answer: Each new identity posts a 70-credit bond to the haven registry and opens a legitimacy market. Anyone may stake for or against it, citing duplicate evidence such as a reused key or reused funds. A zephyr check confirms the bond and an unlisted key. At epoch close, a gale review replays that evidence publicly; a proven fake loses its bond, and its for-stakes go to against-stakers. An honest identity recovers its bond and pays only a 10-credit fee. The k-th fake still risks 80, so 1,000 fakes risk 80,000, no bulk discount. A self-betting ring staking 30 per clone loses 110 per clone if exposed.
